title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. Some vehicles may set P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.

The PCV hose at the elbow looks fine, and I can't hear any hiss even when I bend it.

title: Lean code under boost from loose charge air pipe
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines, model years 2017-2022. P0171 may set during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal. Inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. Repair: reseat the pipe and install a new clamp.

title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

title: Hot restart delay from fuel pump driver module heat soak
text: Applies to 5.3L V8 engines, model years 2022-2024. After towing or extended idling in hot weather, the electronic fuel pump driver module can overheat and delay fuel pump prime on restart. Check the module connector for heat discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Repair: relocate the module with the service kit.

title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
text: Applies to 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2013-2019. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

title: Misfire with ticking at idle from collapsed lifter
text: Applies to 5.3L V8 engines, model years 2022-2024. A misfire code with a ticking noise at idle may indicate a collapsed valve lifter. Perform a relative compression test and listen for lifter noise at idle. Repair: replace the affected lifters and the camshaft as required.

title: Misfire at low-speed high load from pre-ignition
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines, model years 2017-2019. A single-cylinder misfire code may set during wide-open throttle acceleration below 2,000 rpm because of low-speed pre-ignition. Check the engine control software level and the oil specification used at the last service. Repair: reprogram the engine control module and change the oil to the specified grade.

title: Overheating at idle from slipping fan clutch
text: Applies to 5.3L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2014-2021. Temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic if the viscous fan clutch slips. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. Repair: replace the fan clutch.

title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
text: Applies to 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2011-2018. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold crossover
text: Applies to 3.6L V6 engines, model years 2021-2023. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at the coolant crossover. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the crossover area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

title: Coolant expelled from reservoir after overheating
text: Applies to 3.5L V6, 3.6L V6 and 5.3L V8 engines, model years 2011-2021. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks. Repair: install the revised reservoir cap and vent hose.

title: Coolant seepage at turbocharger coolant line
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines, model years 2017-2019. Slow coolant loss may come from the turbocharger coolant return line fitting, which leaves a white crust on the turbo heat shield. Inspect the fitting and heat shield with the engine cold. Repair: replace the coolant line and sealing washers.

title: No heat from rear auxiliary heater
text: Applies to minivans with rear auxiliary heat, model years 2011-2019. The front heater works normally but the rear vents blow cool because the rear heater control valve sticks closed. Command the rear heat on and feel both rear heater hoses under the vehicle. Repair: replace the rear heater control valve.

title: Low heater output at idle from auxiliary coolant pump
text: Applies to 2.4L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with an electric auxiliary coolant pump. Heater output may drop at idle in cold weather when the auxiliary pump does not run. Command the pump on with a scan tool and listen for operation at the pump. Repair: replace the auxiliary coolant pump.

title: Passenger side cold on dual-zone climate control
text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. Heat may be normal on the driver side while the passenger side blows cool, caused by the passenger blend door actuator losing its calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate or replace the passenger blend door actuator.

title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

title: Battery drain from telematics module
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.3L V8, model years 2022-2024. The telematics module may stay awake after a cellular network change and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check for the module staying awake. Repair: update the telematics module software.

title: No-start in extreme cold
text: Applies to all vehicles. In temperatures below 0 deg F, a battery that is healthy in mild weather may not crank the engine after sitting overnight, with no parasitic draw present. Check the battery temperature rating and whether a block heater is fitted and used. Repair: install a higher CCA battery or a battery warmer.

title: Low state of charge on short trips with auto start-stop
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2020-2022. Vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes may show a low battery message because the battery monitoring sensor limits charging. Check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. Repair: update the body control software and reset the sensor.

title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2021-2023. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2020-2022. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

title: Battery lamp at cold startup with belt squeal
text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. Below 10 deg F, the battery warning lamp may light for the first minute after a cold start with a short belt squeal, and it clears once the engine warms. Inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. Repair: install the revised tensioner.

title: No crank when key fob is not detected
text: Applies to small crossovers with push-button start, model years 2023-2025. The engine may not crank and a key-not-detected message appears when the fob battery is weak. Hold the fob against the start button while pressing it to start. Repair: replace the fob battery.

title: Slow crank after hot soak from starter heat
text: Applies to all vehicles. The engine may turn over slowly, but does turn over, when restarted after a hot soak. Measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp during cranking with fuel disabled. Repair: install a starter heat shield or replace the starter.

title: No crank from clutch pedal position switch
text: Applies to vehicles with a manual transmission. The starter may not engage when the clutch pedal switch does not close fully with the pedal pressed. Check switch continuity with the pedal fully depressed. Repair: adjust or replace the clutch pedal position switch.

title: Intermittent no crank from starter relay in underhood fuse block
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.3L V8, model years 2022-2024. The starter may intermittently fail to engage because of a weak starter relay in the underhood fuse block. Swap the starter relay with an identical relay and retest. Repair: replace the starter relay.

title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

title: Pedal pulsation at low speed on rough roads from ABS activation
text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. A pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound may occur during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement because of early ABS activation. Inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. Repair: replace the affected hub and tone ring.

title: Brake vibration while towing
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.3L V8, model years 2022-2024. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

title: Drift to the right on crowned roads
text: Applies to all vehicles. The vehicle may drift to the right while cruising on crowned roads, with no change when the brakes are applied. Check front camber and caster side to side against the alignment specification. Repair: adjust the cross-caster within specification.

title: Pull under hard acceleration
text: Applies to 1.5L turbo I4 engines with front-wheel drive, model years 2017-2022. A pull to one side may occur under hard acceleration from a stop and disappear when coasting or braking. Inspect the engine mounts and inner axle joint for wear. Repair: install the revised lower engine mount.

title: Brake pull from caliper bracket casting
text: Applies to midsize SUVs, model years 2023-2025. A pull during braking may occur because of a front caliper bracket casting variation that holds the outer pad off-center. Inspect the bracket part number stamp against the bulletin list. Repair: replace both front caliper brackets.

title: Hard brake pedal at idle from booster check valve
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2014-2017. The brake pedal may feel hard and require high effort at idle because the brake booster check valve sticks. Measure vacuum at the booster with the engine idling. Repair: replace the booster check valve and hose.

title: Spongy pedal after ABS module replacement
text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. After the ABS hydraulic unit has been replaced or opened, air may remain trapped in the module and produce a spongy pedal. Perform the scan-tool automated bleed procedure. Repair: complete the automated bleed and a conventional bleed.

title: Pedal fade on long downhill grades
text: Applies to all vehicles. The pedal may get progressively softer during repeated hard stops on long downhill grades or while towing, and return to normal after the brakes cool. Check pad compound and fluid boiling point. Repair: install severe-duty pads and flush the fluid.

title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2014-2021. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

title: Clicking or clunk at full steering lock
text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, may come from a worn outer CV joint. Inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. Repair: replace the axle shaft.

title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

title: Steering wheel shake only when braking from highway speed
text: Applies to all vehicles. A steering wheel shake that occurs only when braking from highway speed, and is absent when cruising, usually comes from front rotor thickness variation. Measure rotor runout and thickness variation. Repair: replace or refinish the front rotors.

title: Vibration under light acceleration from rear driveshaft
text: Applies to small crossovers with all-wheel drive, model years 2023-2025. A vibration felt in the floor at 40-50 mph under light acceleration may come from rear driveshaft imbalance. Check driveshaft runout at the center bearing. Repair: install the balanced replacement driveshaft.

title: Steering wheel vibration at idle in gear
text: Applies to all vehicles. A steering wheel vibration felt only at idle in drive with the brake applied, which goes away in neutral, usually comes from a collapsed engine mount. Inspect the mounts with the engine idling in gear. Repair: replace the affected mount.

title: Warm air from rear AC only
text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2011-2019. The front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm because the rear expansion valve sticks closed. Compare front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. Repair: replace the rear expansion valve.

title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2023-2025. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

title: CVT judder on light acceleration
text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. A judder or shudder may be felt during light acceleration from 15-35 mph. Check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Repair: replace the CVT fluid and update the control software.

title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Repair: update the transmission control software.

title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.3L V8, model years 2022-2024. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.
